one_liner: On-site specialist at Fort Belvoir who coaches DoD child-care and youth staff to include children with disabilities and behavioral or medical needs.
fit_summary: This is a specialized child development and special education role that requires 24 semester hours of directly related coursework, proof of education at application, and hands-on skills such as functional behavioral assessments and practice-based coaching. Nothing on file shows Daniel has that education or experience with children. Daniel's people skills and policy knowledge help only with the family and partnership parts of the job.
eligibility: Open to the public (NAF position). No status is needed, but NAF priority goes to current or former NAF employees and to veterans and their spouses or parents.

Education: a bachelor's degree with at least 24 semester hours in special education, early childhood education, child/adolescent development, or a closely related field, OR 24 such hours plus comparable experience. General psychology and sociology courses do not count.
Proof of education (transcripts) must be submitted with the application.
You must also show experience in child development, early intervention, special education, functional behavioral assessments, and knowledge of IDEA and the Rehabilitation Act of 1973.
You must live within 100 miles or 2 hours of Fort Belvoir after accepting. Manassas meets this.
strategy: Check your transcript first. Apply only if you can document 24 semester hours in the listed child, education, or family fields, because general courses are excluded and proof is required at the time of application.
If you lack that coursework, skip this posting. Look instead at DLA or FEMA emergency management, program analyst, or public affairs roles that match your IEM background.
If you do qualify, describe any work with children with special needs, including volunteer work, with dates and hours per week. Aim to show the highly preferred 2 years.
Frame your IEM work around facilitating training for adult learners, coordinating with community agencies, and analyzing program data to brief leadership, but only where that is true.
Keep the resume to two pages, mirror the eight numbered qualifications, and answer the questionnaire honestly, since answers are checked against your resume.
resume_bullets: Facilitated [number] trainings for [audience of adult learners] on [topic] at IEM, using [method] to assess learning and adjust delivery.
Collected and analyzed [quantitative/qualitative data] for [government client program], identified [trend], and presented recommendations to [leadership level].
Built partnerships with [number/type of community agencies or stakeholders] to coordinate [service or plan], supporting [outcome you can document].
interview_questions: Walk us through how you would conduct a functional behavioral assessment and build a Behavior Support Plan with a team.
How do IDEA and Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act apply in a child development center?
Describe how you coach a staff member using practice-based coaching.
Tell us about a difficult conversation with a family and how you kept the partnership strong.
watch_outs: The strict education requirement (24 directly related semester hours, documented) is likely disqualifying unless you have that coursework.
Expect to spend at least 50% of your time in classrooms with children ages six weeks to 18, which is far from policy work.
Promotion potential is none, and NAF priority categories may place outside non-veteran applicants lower in consideration.
